title: SQL vs NoSQL
summary: Relational vs non-relational trade-offs, ACID vs BASE, the main NoSQL families, when each fits, and why the honest answer is usually 'it depends on the access pattern'.
note:
1. SQL: fixed schema, relations, joins, ACID transactions, strong consistency
2. NoSQL families: key-value, document, wide-column, graph
3. ACID (correctness-first) vs BASE (availability-first, eventual consistency)
4. Choose by access pattern + consistency need, not by hype
   • money/relations/ad-hoc queries → SQL
   • huge scale, flexible/denormalised data, simple lookups → NoSQL
✎ In my words: ______________________________________________

recall.q: ACID vs BASE in one line?
recall.a: ACID = correctness-first transactions with strong consistency; BASE = availability-first with eventual consistency.

recall.q: Name the four main NoSQL families.
One clear case each for SQL and NoSQL?
recall.a: SQL for money/relational data needing transactions and ad-hoc joins; NoSQL for massive scale with simple, denormalised, high-write access patterns.

shot.title: NoSQL families
shot.body:
| family | example use | shape |
|---|---|---|
| key-value | sessions, cache | key → blob |
| document | catalog, profiles | JSON docs |
| wide-column | time series, feeds | rows of sparse columns |
| graph | social, fraud | nodes + edges |

sections.title: Relational (SQL)
sections.body: ✍️ Data in tables with a fixed schema and relationships; query with SQL and **joins**. Strong **ACID** transactions make it the default for money, inventory, and anything needing correctness and ad-hoc querying. Scaling writes beyond one machine is harder (needs sharding).

sections.title: Non-relational (NoSQL)
sections.body: ✍️ Schema-flexible stores built to scale out horizontally. Families: **key-value** (Redis/Dynamo — fast lookups, sessions), **document** (MongoDB — nested JSON records), **wide-column** (Cassandra — huge write-heavy tables), **graph** (Neo4j — relationship-centric queries). You usually denormalise and design tables around one query shape.

sections.title: ACID vs BASE
sections.body:
✍️ **ACID:** Atomic, Consistent, Isolated, Durable — correctness-first, typically strong consistency. **BASE:** Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent — availability-first, accepts temporary staleness (ties back to CAP/PACELC).
- Pick ACID when a wrong value is unacceptable; BASE when availability and scale matter more than instant consistency.

sections.title: How to choose
sections.body:
✍️ Decide by **access pattern** and **consistency need**, not by trend. Relational joins and transactions, moderate scale → SQL. Massive scale, simple key lookups or denormalised documents, high write volume, flexible schema → NoSQL. Polyglot persistence (SQL for orders, Redis for sessions, a search index for text) is common.
```java
// Pick the store per workload
orders = postgres;   // transactional, relational
sessions = redis;    // ephemeral key-value
activityFeed = cassandra; // write-heavy, denormalised
```
